articleTitle: Artificial intelligence-based human gesture tracking control techniques of Tello EDU Quadrotor Drone
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology (GEn-CITy 2023)
abstract: This paper comprehensively reviews significant research on various artificial intelligence-based human gesture tracking techniques for the Tello EDU quadrotor drone. The gestures derived from image acquisition techniques include hand, eye, face, and body. Further, the methods include signal acquisition through leap motion and an electroencephalogram. The framework for developing the algorithm with various gestures is also demonstrated. The review table presents a thorough overview of the studies linked to the various human gesture-based techniques. It encompasses details such as the algorithm type, quantity of poses and landmarks, programming language, hardware and framework employed, and validation particulars. Furthermore, it comprehensively analyzes potential areas for future research and improvements within this field.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of OCI and Google Cloud platform for the system of the University of Santo Tomas
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology (GEn-CITy 2023)
abstract: The University of Santo Tomas has decided to migrate their student information system over to the cloud. The Student Information System is part of the university's logistical infrastructure that allows administrators to keep track of student records. The aim is to explore other options that may better cater to the university's SIS system. The study explores Google Cloud Platform (GCP) as a competitor and compares it to Oracle Cloud. The study performs a partial replication of the OCI SIS development configuration done by the STePs and replicates the configuration over to the GCP. Several smokescreen tests are done to test the functionality of the 2 platforms and benchmark tests to analyze the performance of the 2 platforms. The data of the tests are then compared based on their functionality, efficiency, reliability, scalability, and security. With these comparisons, along with the provided documentations of the vendors, a feasibility is also performed. The feasibility study goes over the technical, economical, and operational feasibility of implementing either of the infrastructures as a service. The researchers were able to list which cloud platform performs better in each category and conclude which is the better performing cloud platform in specific categories and overall. With these findings the researchers were able to perform a feasibility study in terms of operational, technical, and economical. Based on the study, with regards to operational feasibility, Google Cloud Platform proves a better choice due to the better performance of their virtual machines. However, in terms of Database the Oracle Cloud Autonomous Database is greatly considered with it handling more transactions per second. With this, the researchers discussed the option for a hybrid implementation among the two platform's services. In terms of technical feasibility, Google Cloud Platform and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure are both functional and the tests prove they would work if needed. But with consideration of the benchmark results, the Google Cloud Platform proved to be the better choice. For economical feasibility, the Google Cloud Platform would be the better choice in terms of service provisions alone, with the assumption that the university does not go over 10 TB of data egress. But anything over the 10 TB of data egress, the Oracle Cloud Infrastructure would be the better option. These results are in respect and may vary over time depending on the currency exchange rate of the US Dollar and Philippine Peso.

articleTitle: Joint segmentation and recognition of melanoma skin lesions via multi-task learning
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology (GEn-CITy 2023)
abstract: Melanoma skin lesion classification and segmentation are two critical tasks for computerized diagnostic systems. These tasks are challenging due to the inherently fuzzy nature and diverse shape variations of skin lesions in dermoscopy images. A joint learning approach has the potential to significantly improve the outcomes of both tasks. This is because there is a strong correlation between skin lesion classification and segmentation. This paper proposes a novel unified multi-task learning approach that facilitates joint segmentation of skin lesion boundaries while simultaneously classifying skin lesion abnormalities. The proposed method incorporates a new regularization technology called joint learning, which promotes mutual benefit between the two tasks by learning shared features and preventing the dominance of one task over the other. The proposed method was evaluated on a publicly dataset called ISIC 2016, involving two different types of skin cancers, benign and melanoma. The experimental results showed that the proposed multi-task learning method has the potential to enhance the overall diagnosis performance of skin cancer analysis. The proposed method achieved an F1 score of 79.94% compared to the single-task learning model's performance of 78.26% while preserving the segmentation capabilities. This study represents a significant stride toward potential generalizability under diverse clinical applications.

articleTitle: Artificial intelligence and the legal profession
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology (GEn-CITy 2023)
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is causing disruptions in nearly every industry and profession, some more quickly and profoundly than others. In contrast to the industrial revolution, which automated physical labor and replaced muscles with hydraulic pistons and diesel engines, the AI-powered revolution is automating mental tasks. While it could be simply streaming a few common positions, simulated intelligence is achieving a more major change to many middle-class jobs that were recently thought to be protected from mechanization. Artificial intelligence (AI) is being used to transform various professions, such as those law, accounting, and IT. It is being used to replace human employees in some cases, and it is also being used to affect the regulation of certain industries. Although it is unlikely that lawyers will be replaced immediately, AI is being used to help them find relevant documents and perform other tasks. In addition, it is being used to help in the drafting of contracts and predict the outcomes of judicial proceedings. AI has been utilized to help with the drafting of contracts, predict legal consequences, and suggest judicial decisions on bail or sentencing.

articleTitle: Language-independent features for detecting fake news: a case study of COVID-19 twitter news feed
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology (GEn-CITy 2023)
abstract: Social media platforms allow users to create and share information instantly. Due to the large amount of information on the social media platforms, some users may not be able to identify fake news. Fake news may be in a form of misinformation or disinformation and can lead to the loss of public trust on certain issues. It is crucial for social media users to detect the presence of fake news efficiently and in a timely manner. This paper aims to investigate the effectiveness of Support Vector Machine (SVM) classification approach to detect Twitter fake news. It is shown that SVM with linear kernel results in good accuracy of around 84% on independent test dataset. Furthermore, linear kernel function outperforms non-linear and polynomial kernel functions.

articleTitle: Comparative study of convolutional neural networks for leaf classification in Ayurveda
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology (GEn-CITy 2023)
abstract: Ayurveda, the traditional system of Indian medicine and healthcare has proven itself over the past centuries. It has grown in acceptance and repute in the eyes of Indians and is also fast spreading to all corners of the world. Herbs are the main essence and are at the core of most ayurvedic medicines. A reduction in the number of experts in the field of identification and sourcing of herbs reduces the quality of medicines. Recognition of herbs through automatic classification of leaves is a remedy for this problem. A vast number of deep learning models for classification of images have emerged in the past decade. This paper makes a comparison between various state-of-the-art convolutional neural networks for classification of leaves. We evaluate architectures including VGG-16, ResNet-50, DenseNet-121, MobileNetV2, EfficientB0 and EfficientV2M. This experiment has been done with a data of 1835 images of leaves taken from 30 different species. ResNet-50, VGG-16, EfficientV2M returned the best result with an accuracy of 98% and EfficientV2M attained the highest accuracy with less number of epochs.

articleTitle: Enhancing the risk management in various sectors through artificial intelligence
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology (GEn-CITy 2023)
abstract: With the Introduction of Industry 4.0 which is all about Artificial intelligence Big data, IoT, robotics etc. every sector of the economy has moved towards technological up gradation, with the increasing complexity of risk in various Industries there is an increasing demand for creative ways to manage the risk. A tool which has the potential to help in the management of various types of risk is Artificial Intelligence. This paper reviews the role of Artificial intelligence in various types of risk management in the commercial world. The paper discusses the benefits of Al in the management of risk, including its ability to analyze risk in real time, accurate predictions and automated process of decision-making. The Study also discusses how various algorithms of Al contribute to risk management. The adoption of Al has proved to be bustling over time to time for the management of risk. Further this paper considers certain challenges faced by Al based risk management system and provides certain recommendations which can be adopted to make it more effective, more secured and transparent.

articleTitle: Rice plants diseases detection and classification using deep learning models
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology (GEn-CITy 2023)
abstract: There has been a 37% yearly decrease in rice yields as a result of rice plant diseases. It might happen mostly as a result of not knowing how to identify and treat diseases that affect rice plants. Plant pathologists are looking for effective and trustworthy techniques to precisely identify and treat diseases affecting rice plants. Farmers still use outdated disease detection methods that require time-consuming visual examinations, leading to unsatisfactory farming operations. Through the use of methods like machine learning and deep learning, which garner a lot of attention in crop disease research, the detection of harmful organisms in rice plants has become substantially more controllable due to improvements in agricultural technology. For these classifications, there are numerous deep learning and machine learning models available, but the real challenge is to propose a method with higher accuracy, precision, recall, etc. Based on the Mandalay dataset of images, this study proposed a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model for the classification of four rice leaf diseases. Additionally, the CNN model's output was compared to that of two previously trained models, namely Resent and Resnet50. It is discovered that the proposed model performs noticeably better than the other two. Compared to previous work, the results are better.

articleTitle: Simulation of Van der Pol equation using state space approach with learning
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology (GEn-CITy 2023)
abstract: This paper proposes a computational approach for solving a Van der Pol equation. Firstly, a simplified model is defined. Then, a loss function, which measures the differences between the Van der Pol equation and the simplified model, is introduced. We aim to minimize the loss function. So, the first-order necessary condition is derived, and a steepest descent recursion equation is obtained to update the state transition matrix. During the iterative procedure, the solution from the state space representation will learn to capture the behaviour of the nonlinear equation, and the optimal state transition matrix can be determined when convergence is achieved. With this, the loss function is minimized. Thus, solving the state space equation will give the solution to the Van der Pol equation, and the computational algorithm is known as the state space learning (SSL) algorithm. For illustration, we consider the parameter in the Van der Pol equation, and the simplified model is solved iteratively using the SSL algorithm. The simulation results show that the iterative solution closely approximates the solution of the Van der Pol equation, and the performance of the SSL algorithm is verified. Finally, the practicality of the SSL algorithm is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Thermal hydraulic analysis in triangular sub-channel for 3MW TRIGA mark II research reactor
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology (GEn-CITy 2023)
abstract: The sub-channel analysis is one of the most efficient ways to calculate heat transfer from the fuel rod to the coolant of the nuclear reactor core either research or power reactor. In this study, a novel strategy is shown for the 3MW Triga Mark II research reactor by creating a Triangular shape subchannel in the solid work software and analyzing its thermal-hydraulic parameters (e.g., temperature profile, pressure drop, velocity profile, etc.) in the ANSYS Fluent program using the Finite Volume Method of the CFD problems. Three different models such as k- epsilon (k-ε), k- ω (k-omega), and Transition SST were used to compare with each other to find the closest solution by generating graphs on temperature, pressure, turbulence eddy viscosity, and turbulent kinetic energy. The nuclear fuel centerline temperature from k-epsilon was found to be 743 K, which was within the safety limit of 950 K for TRIGA fuel rods and validates with the safety analysis report of the TRIGA reactor. The heat transfer coefficient was found to be 19748.13 W/m2 K for the k-epsilon model which is greater than other methods.

articleTitle: Performance comparison of machine learning and neural network for sitting posture detection among university students
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology (GEn-CITy 2023)
abstract: Sitting occupies more hours of the day especially for typical adults due to the global Covid-19 pandemic. Research had shown that prolonged sitting is unhealthy, which may lead to health concerns such as musculoskeletal pain. Therefore, sitting adults should aware and notified if there is any improper sitting posture. This work was conducted to detect a person's current spinal position over a period of time using tri-axial accelerometers. The data collected from sensors were processed and classified using Machine Learning (ML) and Neural Network (NN) classifiers. By extracting axial displacements between sensors, spinal movements can be determined. Data was collected from a total of fourteen university students using the constructed sensing circuitry and were transferred to Matlab for processing. The results achieved accuracies of 93.7% and 96.7% for ML and NN, respectively.

articleTitle: Design of transmission quality prediction procedures on coarse wavelength division multiplexing with 4-channel transmission using machine learning
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology (GEn-CITy 2023)
abstract: An optical network is a high-capacity telecommunication network using optical technology and components. CWDM is usually used in optical networks in urban areas because CWDM has a wide bandwidth and follows the needs of urban areas that only need short distances. Machine learning (ML) is a branch of artificial intelligence that is very suitable for dealing with complex problems that are difficult to answer in a reasonable time. Accurate Quality of Transmission (QoT) prediction before the connection establishment is critical for service provision and network resource utilization. The Coarse Wavelength Division Multiplexing (CWDM) model used by the network is by the ITU-T G.694.2 standard, namely a splitting of 20 nm at the wavelengths listed in the standard 1551 nm, 1571 nm, 1591 nm, and 1611 nm. The approach used is a linear regression algorithm with an accuracy of 82.47%, k-nearest neighbor regression with an accuracy of 77.18%, support vector regression with an accuracy of 83.88%, random forest regression of 91.44%, and ANN regression with an accuracy of 94.52%. The random forest regressor is the best machine learning algorithm for predicting transmission quality because even though it has lower accuracy, its computation time far exceeds ANN regression, which is only 1.9098 ms.

articleTitle: Aircraft recognition using convolutional neural network
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology (GEn-CITy 2023)
abstract: Satellite image object-recognition offers detailed location representation where ground-based sampling is limited or inaccessible, such as high sea or in the mountains. However, an accurate and effective method is required to ensure the precision of the information generated due to small, ambiguous objects against the background. Having an automatic object detection system would greatly speed up satellite image recognition and find extensive applications in defense, transportation, agriculture, and emergency relief. With the advancement of artificial neural networks, the technology has seen applications in various fields from image processing to speech synthesis. We aimed to develop a neural network-based commercial aircraft detection system on satellite images at major airports. We proposed a R-CNN-based aircraft recognition system where CNN is utilized to extract features of aircraft before passing the feature maps to the binary classifier. We trained the model with 2100 images of satellite images containing aircraft which are segmented to produce positive and negative instances and validated on 900 images. The system is equipped to detect and localize the position of the aircraft in an image while registering excellent accuracy. However, as the number of aircraft in a frame increases, slight deterioration in the model performance is observed.

articleTitle: Investigation of Electric Vehicle (EV) and Renewable Energy Sources (RES) for low voltage distribution network in Malaysia
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology (GEn-CITy 2023)
abstract: The transportation sector is ranked the second highest in carbon emission in Malaysia due to the massive amount of fossil fuel usage for vehicles. The situation worsens as most Malaysians relies heavily on personal vehicles due to the poor public transportation system in in the country. Electrical Vehicle (EV) with zero emission is a good replacement for fossil fuel vehicle. However, EV integration triggers a series of problems in the low voltage distribution network where the EV is charged. The objective of this project includes implementing an EV load model into a small distribution network in Malaysia and add a distributed generation with renewable energy into the network to reduce the impact of EV. Data from an actual distribution network was taken from literature and the utility supplier's handbook in Malaysia. A solar system was selected as the location of the distribution network is at the residential area. The EV load rating and plug-in time of this paper is 3.3kW and 7 p.m. respectively. Simulation tool was used to model the distribution network and the EV load. Next, the renewable energy system was modelled based on a combination of literature study and empirical methods. The simulation result yields a 217.83% loading and -4.6% voltage sag for one of the transformers in the distribution network. After integration of renewable energy, the result show improved stability where the system loading is 70% with a voltage sag of -1.23%.

articleTitle: Design of a WDM system with radio over free space optics for 5G fronthaul networks in an urban area
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology (GEn-CITy 2023)
abstract: 5G radio-optical network, or 5G-RON, is one scenario that implements a cloud radio access network (C-RAN) architecture. In fronthaul networks, to be able to meet delay and capacity requirements, optical cables can be used. Free space optic technology has become an alternative medium for optical cables to meet fronthaul needs on 5G networks. The atmosphere affects the transmission quality, so wavelength division multiplexing (WDM) technology increases bandwidth and large bit rates in a network. This study discusses the design and performance analysis of the WDM-based RoFSO system for implementing 5G networks in Kemayoran, Central Jakarta, Indonesia, conducted using Optisystem for 4 WDM channels at 1490 nm, 1510 nm, 1530 nm, and 1550 nm. The tests were carried out using a 10 Gbps bit rate. This research was conducted to see meteorological effects that use data from the Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics Agency. The signal output at high attenuation will cause a more limited transmission distance. The use of high rainfall as attenuation in one year can only reach 0.8 km. The wavelength also affects the signal quality due to interference that degrades the signal quality.

articleTitle: Environmental localization and detection using 2D LIDAR on a non-holonomic differential mobile robot
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology (GEn-CITy 2023)
abstract: This research presents a novel approach for environmental localization and multi-object detection using a 2D LIDAR system integrated into a non-holonomic differential mobile robot. The proposed methodology combines SLAM real-time localization and Euclidean Clustering for detecting surrounding objects, enabling the robot to localize effectively within its working environment and identify multiple obstacles. By segmenting LIDAR data into discrete object clusters, the system can accurately determine the size and shape of detected obstacles, providing a detailed understanding of the environment. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach effectively addresses the challenges of localization and multi-object detection. The Euclidean Clustering approach has shown to be a lot more effective. With a time performance of 443.1677 seconds, it finishes the mission. The Euclidean clustering is significantly faster than the K-Nearest Neighbors (K-NN) technique, which required 11256 seconds with a K value of 100 and 16542 seconds with a K value of 200. The performance of autonomous mobile robots is improved because Euclidean Clustering provides a better time performance in these specific scenarios.

articleTitle: Solving Hamiltonian path problem using DNA computing
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology (GEn-CITy 2023)
abstract: Hamiltonian path problem is a combinatorial problem. This problem requires an exponential time to compute using traditional computing methods and algorithms. There is a way of reducing the computational time from exponential to polynomial time by connecting the ending vertex with the starting vertex creating a Hamiltonian Cycle. But we wanted to solve the Hamiltonian path problem. The Hamiltonian path for a small graph is easy to find. But, for a graph with numerous vertices, it is hard to find. Traditional computers take a long time to solve this problem. So, we need parallel computing to solve such a problem. One substance in nature has the ability to compute parallelly. DNA molecules are capable to compute parallelly. We have done some work on this to find the solution to this problem. We have conducted the test and successfully can generate a Hamiltonian path from any kind of graph. For small problems, this approach is not efficient, but for large problems, DNA molecules work way better.

articleTitle: Analysing weather conditions using Firebase
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology (GEn-CITy 2023)
abstract: Forecasting Weather to a specific time and location via the use of science and technology for its specific location from the 19th century, millions of humans have started predicting weather forecasting. This technology uses meteorology so that it predicts the weather for the future so that the response of the atmosphere can be recorded for the future purpose. Technology for predicting weather we use barometric pressure, in that which show the current weather condition and cloud cover for Sky condition this prediction model is based on the Computer Based model show the records of a wide range of atmospheric will be recorded by having this technology for model prediction is pattern recognition, telecommunication model, performance knowledge, but its skill required the more in this technology for forecasting the chaotic character of the weather which is overpowered by the measurement error by this less accuracy the atmospheric dynamic model field to predicting the model which is already exist for forecasting.
